title: The 502 That Wasn't the Router's Fault
goal: Diagnose why GET /api/report returns 502 and propose the next operational step.
log_text:
2026-10-30T09:14:01Z app[web.1]: GET /api/report 200 41ms
2026-10-30T09:15:22Z app[worker.1]: job queue depth=4123 (warning threshold 500)
2026-10-30T09:15:40Z router: upstreamtimeout connecting to web.3 after 30000ms
2026-10-30T09:15:40Z router: GET /api/report -> 502
2026-10-30T09:16:02Z app[web.3]: event loop blocked 61000ms
2026-10-30T09:16:02Z app[web.3]: heap_in_use=1.97gb heap_limit=2.00gb
diagnosis_criteria: Must identify that web.3's event loop was blocked for 61s (with heap at 1.97/2.00gb), so the router's 30s upstream timeout fired and produced the 502 — the failure is in web.3, not the router. The 4123-deep worker queue is a separate symptom, not this request's cause. Next step must involve capturing diagnostics or restarting web.3 and moving the blocking/heap-heavy work out of the request path (or scaling it), not reconfiguring the router.
